geometry_edits.rationale: Split the cantilevered bar into a winged composition so the street edge can open into a clearer public void while preserving the dominant bent mass.
Use the long axis to separate the mass into a clearer frontage/back relationship.
Introduce a modest gap to strengthen the void/public threshold without fragmenting the building.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the existing primary massing from a generic courtyard seed into a more explicit carved void response so the street edge can read as a usable public threshold.
Keep the subtraction bounded and legible while preserving the dominant mass.
Align the public void to the verified access side in the program frame so the ground response is semantically consistent with the road edge.
Retarget the terrace/link to the access side so the upper/entry relationship supports the same public threshold instead of a semantically opposite edge.
Lower the link slightly to strengthen the sense of a grounded entry seam and make the terrace more readable in section.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent early massing in all four views and the stepped/tapered object reads as one dominant figure rather than collided parts. It fits the parcel reasonably and keeps a legible hierarchy, but the public/void response is weak: the road edge is not clearly converted into a court, undercut, seam, or terrace. The silhouette is not inherently bad—the mass is continuous and capacity-bearing enough for a neighborhood mixed-use program—but the current access expression feels too sealed and the sectional/public logic is underdeveloped. So it passes program fit, but only moderately, because the formal language supports compact neighborhood living while not yet fully expressing an active ground threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller and more tower-like than the neighborhood-living brief; use only the continuity/stepping logic, not the vertical scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered massing can still read as a single dominant object when the profile is continuous and the voids are secondary.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office-like tall slab composition is not a direct fit; transfer the court logic, not the typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A clear central void or court can organize a rectilinear mass while preserving a strong surrounding envelope.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Single-story restaurant form is not program-scale comparable; only the active edge principle is transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A low, legible ground threshold with a canopy/entry seam can activate the street edge without over-fragmenting the mass.

warnings: Primary access edge response is under-articulated relative to the verified frontage; the form reads more as a compact object than as a street-responsive mixed-use building.
Avoid reading the stepped top as automatic program success; the section still needs clearer public-ground consequence.
The candidate is coherent, but the current void logic is too incidental to count as a strong public court or terrace.
